title: Selling the Paramount banjo and later the guitar
summary: He regrets trading in his Paramount banjo for $25, and later sold the guitar to bandleader Larry Vecca.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Yeah. To prove it, I'll tell you one thing which I always regretted. I had a good banjo which I said I bought second hand for $75. And after I played the banjo for those number of years, as I mentioned before, and I went to Whirlines and I traded in my banjo on a stake string guitar, a good Epiphone guitar. Whirlines gave me $25 on that banjo. If I had that banjo today I could sell it for $500.

It was a Paramount banjo. You see banjos came back in the late years and became real popular. But between 28 and 32 banjos were popular and then around 32, nearly everybody played banjos, switched to six string guitar and banjos dwindled down slightly for a few years. So in order to keep up with the times I got me a six string guitar and started working on that. And then when I bought my string bass in 37 at Whirlines, I said well I'm not going to make that mistake again. I put that six string guitar under the bed in a plush line case that I bought at Whirlines. And I said I'm going to leave that under the bed and when my daughters get old enough maybe they'll want to play it. You see? I wasn't going to go to Whirlines and get $25 on that. So you know that bass laid under that bed in that case for 12 years and the daughters never did get interested in playing that because I said before one studied clarinet and got the scholarship to a Dominican high school. And then years later they both studied piano. So then my wife says Bob why don't you sell your guitar, the kids are not going to fool with it. So I put an ad in the paper and I sold a guitar for $125 to a friend of mine who had a guitar exactly like it and he had dropped it and cracked it. So I got to earn $25 for the guitar. Who was it that bought it?
Yeah, a musician friend of mine by the name of Larry Vecca who recently passed away, I think he passed away two or three years ago. He had his own band.
Yeah from a famous family too. Larry Vecca.
His father played with Jack Lane. He's a Vecca also that plays piano. He used to work at the Times for Keown. He's related to Larry Vecca.
I've never met any of them but Jack Lane used to talk about the Lawrence who was the father
I guess. Yeah. Larry Vecca. Well Larry used to have a big nine, ten, twelve piece band and he operated for many years. And he, my friend, he saw the ad in the paper he came up and grabbed the guitar.
